{{ (() => { const config = $('Config').first().json; const sheets = $('Fetch Data and Schema Sheets').first().json.sheets || []; const dataSheet = sheets.find(s => s.properties?.title === config.data_sheet_name); const row0 = dataSheet?.data?.[0]?.rowData?.[0]; return row0 ? (row0.values || []).map(cell => { const uev = cell?.userEnteredValue; if (!uev) return ''; return uev.stringValue ?? uev.numberValue ?? uev.boolValue ?? ''; }) : []; })() }}

Generate a schema definition for each column. Output a JSON array where each item has:
- ColumnName: the exact column name (preserve case)
- Type: one of [str, int, date, list, class]
- Description: brief description (10 words max) of what this field stores
- Classes: if Type is "class", provide 2-4 comma-separated enum values; otherwise empty string

Type guidelines:
- date: timestamps, birthdays, created_at, updated_at, any date field
- int: IDs, counts, frequencies, ages, numeric identifiers
- list: multiple values (emails, phones, jobs, tags, anything plural)
- class: categorical/status fields (use Classes for enum values)
- str: everything else (names, addresses, notes, single text values)

IMPORTANT: Output ONLY the JSON array, no explanation.

parameters.content:
## Extract data from a Drive folder into Google Sheets

Turn a folder of invoices, receipts, CVs or scans into a table: one row per file, filled into the columns you already have.

### How it works
1. Reads your sheet's header row and, on first run, has an LLM draft a schema sheet describing each column.
2. Lists the Drive folder and skips files already written successfully, so a rerun resumes where the last one stopped.
3. Downloads each file and sends it to the any-file2json-converter sub-workflow (PDF, images, Office, CSV, JSON, text).
4. Writes one row per file, matched to your column names.
5. A file that fails still gets a row, with `extraction_status` giving the reason. After the last file the run fails with that list, so your error workflow sees it. The next run retries only those files.

### Setup steps
- [ ] Import and publish [any-file2json-converter](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/03_any-file2json-converter/workflows/any-file2json-converter.json) first
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet whose header row names the fields you want (e.g. Date, Amount, Vendor)
- [ ] Connect Google Drive and Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials
- [ ] Connect an LLM credential to **Schema LLM**
- [ ] Set `folder_id` and `spreadsheet_id` in **Config**
- [ ] Re-select your converter in **Convert File to Text**

### Customization
- Edit the schema sheet to change a column's type, description or allowed values.
- `file_include`, `file_exclude`, `file_limit` and `max_file_size_mb` in **Config** narrow a run.
- Hitting LLM rate limits? Raise `rate_limit_wait_seconds`. The rerun skips finished files.

[Full setup guide](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/02_smart-table-fill/docs/setup-guide-folder2table.md) · [Project page](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/02_smart-table-fill/README.md) · Text instead of files? [smart-table-fill](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/02_smart-table-fill/workflows/smart-table-fill.n8n.json)

## After import
Set `folder_id`, `spreadsheet_id` and `data_sheet_name` (your tab's name) here. Every other field has a working default.

## Build the extraction schema
Reads your sheet headers. On first run an LLM writes a schema sheet (type, description, allowed values per column). Edit it to steer extraction.

## Pick files to process
Adds missing helper columns, lists the folder and skips files already written successfully.

## Stops here?
A `class` column has an empty `Classes` cell in the schema sheet. Add comma-separated values, or change its Type to `str`.

## Inputs
extraction:
`{{ $json._extraction || $('Build Output Schema and Filter').first().json._extraction || {} }}`

## After import
Select **your** imported [converter](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/03_any-file2json-converter/workflows/any-file2json-converter.json) here. If `extraction` is blank, restore it from the blue note.

## Write one row per file
Parses the converter output into your columns. A failed file still gets a row with `extraction_status` ([what each value means](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/02_smart-table-fill/docs/setup-guide-folder2table.md#when-a-file-fails)).

## Loop: 1 file at a time
If file #6 fails, files 1-5 are already written
and a rerun skips them.
After the last file, **Check for Failed Files**
fails the run if any file failed.

## Rate limits
Raise `rate_limit_wait_seconds`, or let an error workflow restart this run with a higher wait. [Example](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/10_error-handler/workflows/mainflow.md#execute-workflow-retry-no-sheet-storage)
